intro: Lesson 110: Revision: P5 density, pressure and gases. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: (a) Describe how to find the density of an irregular object [3]. (b) A diver is at 12 m in sea water (ρ = 1030 kg/m³). Calculate the extra pressure [2]. (c) A bubble of 2.0 cm³ at that depth (total pressure 224 kPa) rises to the surface (100 kPa). Calculate its new volume at constant temperature [3].
questions.a: (a) mass on a balance (1); volume by displacement in a measuring cylinder or eureka can (1); ρ = m ÷ V (1); (b) p = 12 × 1030 × 10 = 123 600 Pa (2); (c) p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ (1); 224 × 2.0 = 100 × V₂ (1); V₂ = 4.48 cm³ (1)
questions.model: Teacher sets out (b): equation, substitution, answer with unit.

questions.q: Explain, using particles, why the pressure in a tyre rises on a hot day.
questions.a: Air molecules gain kinetic energy/move faster (1); collide with walls more often (1) and with more force (1)

questions.q: Why must temperatures be in kelvin for p/T = constant?
questions.a: Pressure is proportional to absolute temperature; °C has an arbitrary zero.

questions.q: A stone has mass 270 g and displaces 100 cm³ of water. Density?
questions.model: Density = mass ÷ volume. Volume from displacement = 100 cm³. 270 ÷ 100 = 2.7 g/cm³.
